analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. These units change documentation only: changelog.d/provider-fast-reconnect.md:3-5 describes a 60-second stability reset and randomized 0-1-second retry for coordinator close 1012; docs/architecture/components/provider.md:119-143 describes recording session duration and close codes, including raw-payload fallback; docs/provider/cli-reference.md patch head:1968-1971 documents the constants. No executable implementation is supplied here, so these claims do not establish runtime correctness.
Against TB-002, TB-011, T-053 and A-018, faster reconnection affects availability and connection turnover, not serving authority. The surrounding lifecycle documentation (provider.md:108-117,145-164) retains fresh socket nonces, teardown of resume state, cancellation of old requests and origin-bound Apple replies. Nothing changed here asserts that reconnection renews authorization or resumes completions. The supplied changes do not alter encryption, key custody, plaintext exposure, cache isolation (T-041), model qualification, billing settlement, fan authority or local add-on controls. No concrete security regression is supported by these documentation changes.
Integration should verify CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, CoordinatorClientState.swift and CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift together: stable-session timing, coordinator-only close-code attribution and bounded payload parsing, recording before transport teardown, jitter/backoff behavior, and cancellation/shutdown responsiveness. Confirm accelerated replacement preserves the documented T-053 connection fencing and T-010 request cancellation. These are material runtime contracts not verified in this documentation-only scope; missing source is a coverage limit, not an observed missing control.
